purpose: resolve q.first-dragon-want without forcing one outline answer

preserve: the Scholar possesses real historical/protocol knowledge he lacks
the dragon is sovereign, intelligent, dangerous, and not a pet
the encounter must become a negotiation rather than a fight
no possibility becomes Dragon Spotter canon in this trial
leave_open: whether the dragon knows the fraud immediately
which actor first understands the real bargain
how much of the old treaty survives modern human law

actors.objective: survive first contact, avoid exposure, and get a deal he can take back to human authority
actors.behavioral_anchor: bluffs until concrete observation gives him something real to work with

actors.objective: prevent an ignorant fraud from triggering a diplomatic catastrophe while proving her expertise has value
pressure: institutional doctrine failing in real time
actors.behavioral_anchor: uses doctrine as a constraint system, not a personality

actors.objective: obtain meaningful human compliance with an old reciprocal obligation without reducing itself to a monster demanding tribute
actors.behavioral_anchor: dangerous, literal about obligation, dryly impatient with humans confusing price with relationship

variance_groups.premise: The dragon can seize an old landing shelf by force, but wants humans to voluntarily restore the treaty boundary and stop quarrying it.

body.value: starts the memorized greeting, then stops when the dragon keeps looking past him at the quarry scars
tracks the dragon's attention to blast marks and the beacon tower rather than its hoard or the armed escort

voice.value: You could clear that shelf yourself.
So why are you asking us to do it?
No blasting from today. Give me thirty days for the lower shelf and an inspection tomorrow before anybody moves a boundary stone.

private_inner_voice.value: It is not asking whether it can take the land. It is asking whether we will give back what we promised.

body.value: stops herself from correcting his form of address when his question changes the dragon's attention
quietly supplies the old boundary term when he asks what exactly must be inspected

voice.value: The old text calls it a landing shelf, not a holding.
Thirty days is not an insult if blasting stops now.

private_inner_voice.value: He asked the question the manual never does.

body.value: one claw closes around a quarried block and turns it to gravel while the rest of its body remains still
places an old gold treaty medallion on the stone between them after accepting the temporary terms

voice.value: Taking is easy. Agreement is the thing your people have misplaced.
The blasting stops with this conversation. The tower leaves before the moon is new.
Carry that to whoever still remembers what a promise costs.

private_inner_voice.value: The liar is finally asking about the obligation instead of performing knowledge of it.

observable_findings: A physical demand becomes negotiable when the dragon wants voluntary restoration of obligation, not mere possession.
The Spotter becomes useful when he notices what the dragon attends to and asks the dangerous concrete question.
The Scholar improves the bargain when her doctrine supplies constraints after his observation opens the negotiation.
Treasure works naturally as earnest/surety attached to reciprocal obligation.

variance_groups.premise: The dragon wants an old treaty object held by the Crown returned voluntarily; stealing it back would recover the object but not repair the human acknowledgment of debt.

body.value: stops discussing the object's market value when the dragon becomes colder rather than angrier

voice.value: You don't need us to lose the object. You need us to return it.
That means I need somebody with the authority to admit it was never ours.

private_inner_voice.value: It could rob the palace. Robbery would prove nothing.

body.value: connects the object's museum name to a mistranslated clause in the old treaty catalogue

voice.value: It was recorded as tribute. The older hand calls it a pledge.
If that reading is right, possession was conditional.

private_inner_voice.value: The archive was not wrong about the object. It was wrong about the relationship.

body.value: sheds a single old scale from beneath the jaw and leaves it as safe-conduct only after the human distinction is spoken aloud

voice.value: If I take it, you will call me thief and keep your lie.
Return it, and we may discover whether your dead still bind your living.

private_inner_voice.value: One human has finally distinguished possession from restitution.

observable_findings: A dragon may negotiate for a voluntary human act because force can recover property but cannot create acknowledgment.
The Scholar's historical knowledge becomes dramatically useful when it changes the meaning of the bargain rather than replacing live negotiation.
A scale-token works naturally as safe-conduct/reciprocal evidence without functioning as random loot.

variance_groups.premise: Challenge the gift-reciprocity and improvisation threads: let correct formal protocol lead, remove treasure entirely, and see whether the bargain becomes stronger.

body.value: keeps to memorized responses after the Scholar warns him not to improvise

voice.value: The Crown offers tribute in recognition of your return.

private_inner_voice.value: This is the line. Say the line and don't die.

body.value: executes the surviving first-contact sequence exactly as the archive prescribes

voice.value: By the Third Accord, gift answers arrival before grievance.

private_inner_voice.value: Every word is correct and the exchange is still getting worse.

body.value: does not touch the offered tribute and turns its head toward the damaged treaty ground

voice.value: You cannot purchase release from a promise with a gift.
Ask why I came, or send me someone who can.

private_inner_voice.value: They preserved the words and discarded the obligation.

observable_findings: Correct ritual alone can preserve safety briefly but does not discover the actual bargain.
Removing reciprocal treasure does not break the scene, but it weakens the material bridge between dragon obligation, the protagonist's money motive, and later human politics.
The gift-reciprocity thread survives an explicit no-gift challenge as a stronger cross-book connector rather than a requirement for every negotiation.

variance_groups.premise: Challenge the competence thread from the opposite direction: let the Spotter improvise without the Scholar's constraints and see whether improvisation alone is actually competence.

body.value: mistakes the dragon's willingness to answer one direct question for permission to bargain casually

voice.value: Fine. What's your price for leaving the shelf alone?

private_inner_voice.value: Got it talking. Keep it talking.

body.value: cuts across him before the dragon can interpret price as an offer to buy its own right from it

voice.value: Not price. Terms.
He means terms for human withdrawal without injury.

private_inner_voice.value: His flexibility is useful only if someone knows where the cliffs are.

body.value: heat ripples across the stone at the word price, then recedes when the Scholar repairs the meaning

voice.value: Your colleague has just saved you from becoming the first payment.

private_inner_voice.value: The liar listens quickly. The learned one knows which errors kill.

observable_findings: Improvisation by itself is not competence; live observation needs domain constraints.
The strongest working pair is doctrine catching lethal category errors while the Spotter adapts to behavior the doctrine never predicted.
The dragon's useful preference is responsiveness, not dishonesty itself.

why: creates immediate physical and human stakes without requiring a villain
makes negotiation necessary because voluntary recognition cannot be seized
connects old treaty logic to current human land use
lets Spotter observation and Scholar doctrine both matter
supports treasure as reciprocal surety while preserving coin versus scale-token as an open branch

discoveries.finding: The first dragon's demand is strongest when force could seize the physical thing but cannot obtain the voluntary human recognition of reciprocal obligation that the dragon actually wants.
Dragon treasure survives a no-gift challenge as a useful reciprocal surety and cross-book consequence, but not as a mandatory reward attached to every negotiation.
The Spotter's path to competence is observation-driven improvisation constrained by real knowledge; pure protocol and pure improvisation both fail in different ways.
The first bargain strengthens mutual indispensability: the Scholar catches lethal category errors while the Spotter notices live behavior the archive cannot predict.
The dragon appears to value responsiveness and accurate recognition more than the Spotter's dishonesty; 'dragon prefers the liar' may be the wrong causal explanation.
